title: Pitch link to pitch plate grip length
description: The grip-length joint as a graph: 6 parts, 9 interfaces, 10 edges. It adds no value and no citation of its own -- if a number here looks wrong, the stack file is where it is wrong.

joint.description: The 5-place joint in DETAIL B: NAS6403U11D bolt down through the pitch-link eye (spherical bearing) and a plain bushing, through a 4.06 mm pitch-plate lug, retained by a slotted nut + cotter pin over a flat washer.
joint.scope: Grip length only, and only along the bolt axis. Out of scope, deliberately: diameter and hole fits; bushing-to-bore interference; the pitch link's own internal stack; the joint at the other end of the pitch link; torque and preload.

provenance.values: NONE are copied. Every edge carries a `dimension_ref` into the stack file above, resolved at load time by tolerance_stack.topology.load_topology, so this document cannot drift away from the numbers that stack publishes. Every value's citation and confidence is whatever that element already carries -- this topology adds no source_ref of its own to any value and closes no gap the stack has open.
provenance.structure: The nodes and the edge orientation are a READING of the stack's element order and roles, not a sourced claim, exactly as topology_vpa_output_to_pitch_plate.json's structure note describes for the L1 proof. The stack's axial order from the bolt head, complete since 2026-09-15 (handoff stack_fable_audit): bushing, pitch-link eye, flanged-bushing flange, pitch-plate lug, washer. Until that date the eye had no element to hang an interface on and the flange was not known to exist, so this topology omitted both and said so here; the stack modelling both (the eye as a loudly-marked placeholder) is what lets this graph carry them without inventing anything the stack does not claim. The bolt's own fastener dimensions (grip, overall length, cotter-hole-to-point) are read as edges sharing additional interfaces beyond the clamped stack's own (the bolt's point, and the cotter-hole centreline), which is what turns this graph into more than L1's single grounded loop: the clamped-stack/grip loop (closing at the derived `shank_out` gap) and the length/grip/thread-region loop (closing at the derived `thread_region` edge), which share the bolt-head interface.
provenance.part_identity: The bolt (NAS6403U11D), the pitch-plate lug (215197) and the washer (NAS1149V0332H) are named on the stack's own citations. The plain bushing (214820-002) is likewise named by the stack's parts-list citation. The pitch link (213862-002) and the flanged bushing (NAS77A3-015A) are named on the stack's 2026-09-15 identifications (216231 A.1 and 215177-A parts lists respectively); the spherical bearing inside the link is the stack's own loudly-marked UNCONFIRMED candidate (MS14101-3). No part identity is invented here that the referenced stack does not already claim.

parts.name: NAS6403U11D bolt, .1900-32, .688 grip
parts.note: Balloon 5X in DETAIL B, per the referenced stack's parts list. A standard part; its dimensional identity is the NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet the referenced elements cite.

parts.name: 214820-002 BUSHING, PLAIN, ALUMINUM BRONZE, .1900 in ID X .1875 in LONG
parts.note: Balloon 8X in DETAIL B per the referenced element's source_ref. The Joby part drawing for 214820-002 is not in this repo -- see the referenced element's own gap note.

parts.name: pitch plate (215197), 5X 4.06 +/-0.10 flange group
parts.note: The referenced element's source_ref names this drawing and zone D10, the 5X group distinct from the 3X (tangential link) and 1X (VPA output) groups on the same sheet.

parts.name: NAS1149V0332H washer, flat, 6Al-4V, .203 x .438 x .032 in
parts.note: Balloon 8X in DETAIL B per the referenced element's source_ref (find 32, qty 9 across the assembly).

parts.name: spherical bearing, internal to 213862-002 PITCH LINK ASSEMBLY -- bearing identity UNCONFIRMED
parts.note: Added 2026-09-15 (handoff stack_fable_audit) with the stack's own pitch_link_eye element. The link assembly is 213862-002 (216231 A.1 parts list, item 24, qty 5); which bearing it swages -- MS14101-3 (narrow, the modelled placeholder) or MS14103-3 (wide) -- is stated by no document in reach and is the referenced element's ranked gap 1. No balloon in DETAIL B: the bearing arrives inside the link assembly, same pattern as the tan-link and VPA bearings.

parts.name: NAS77A3-015A BUSHING, FLANGED, PRESS FIT, ALUMINUM BRONZE, ALUMINUM COATED, .1900 in ID
parts.note: Added 2026-09-15 (handoff stack_fable_audit). Press-fit into the pitch plate assembly (215177-A parts list find 2, qty 8 = 3 tangential-link + 5 pitch-link lugs), which is why DETAIL B balloons no flanged bushing. Only its FLANGE is an edge here: the barrel sits inside the plate bore, parallel to the lug, and the referenced stack has no bore-depth path -- unlike the tan-link take-2 topology, which models the barrel and its chamfer for that stack's bore path.

nodes.name: bolt-head bearing face against the plain bushing
nodes.note: Where the grip is measured from: NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet 2 note (a) defines grip as underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical shank, per the referenced fastener elements' source_ref.

nodes.name: plain bushing face against the pitch-link eye (spherical bearing ball)
nodes.note: Replaced `bushing_pitch_plate_face` on 2026-09-15 (handoff stack_fable_audit): that interface was a reading that reproduced the stack's then-incomplete arithmetic (the eye was omitted for want of any source) and its own note said it did not assert the bushing and the lug actually touch. They do not -- the eye and the flange sit between, same architecture as the tan-link joint.

nodes.name: pitch-link eye face against the flanged bushing's flange
nodes.note: Added 2026-09-15 (stack_fable_audit); mirrors the tan-link take-2 topology's bearing_flanged_bushing_face.

nodes.name: flanged bushing flange face against the pitch-plate lug
nodes.note: Added 2026-09-15 (stack_fable_audit). The flange bears on the lug face; the bushing's barrel passes into the lug's bore (not modelled -- no bore-depth path in the referenced stack).

nodes.name: pitch-plate lug face against the flat washer
flat washer far face -- the last modelled clamped surface
nodes.note: A datum_feature and not a mate: beyond it sits the slotted nut (MS9363-09) and cotter pin (MS24665-153), deliberately outside this joint's scope, exactly as topology_vpa_output_to_pitch_plate.json's bushing_far_face is.

nodes.name: end of the bolt's full cylindrical shank
nodes.note: The grip's far end, defined by NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet 2 note (a). Not a mate: it is where the thread run-out begins.

nodes.name: bolt point (tip)
nodes.note: The far end of `bolt_length_11` (head bearing face to point) and the near end of `cotter_hole_from_point` (cotter-hole centreline to bolt point).

nodes.name: cotter-pin hole centreline
nodes.note: NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet 1, dimension M, read off the figure per the referenced element's own source_ref note.

edges.name: pitch-link eye: spherical bearing ball width (bearing identity UNCONFIRMED)
edges.note: Added 2026-09-15 (stack_fable_audit). The referenced element is the repo's loudest placeholder -- MS14101-3's catalog band, `untraced`, awaiting the 213862-002 drawing -- and this edge inherits every caveat on it.

edges.name: fastener grip, NAS6403U11D (.688 in)
edges.note: Runs PARALLEL to the clamped stack rather than in series with it. Together with `shank_out` it closes the loop `study_pitch_link_shank_out.json` sums.

edges.name: NAS6403U11D overall length, head bearing face to point (1.011 in)
edges.note: Runs PARALLEL to `fastener_grip` + `thread_region` (together they close the loop `study_pitch_link_thread_region_t.json` sums) and to `cotter_hole_from_point` reversed (together with the clamped stack, the loop `study_pitch_link_cotter_hole_clearance.json` sums).

edges.name: cotter-hole centreline to bolt point (dimension M)
shank out -- full-diameter shank beyond the modelled clamped stack
edges.note: A DERIVED gap: it carries no dimension because it is the quantity `study_pitch_link_shank_out.json` computes. Its endpoints share no part (the washer, the bolt), so it is kind `gap` rather than a structural dimension. This is check `shank_out__11_sourced_only`'s own residual, and per that check's own guidance the missing pitch-link eye is what would need to fill it.

edges.name: thread run-out and point region beyond the full-diameter shank
edges.note: A DERIVED edge -- carries no dimension. Both its interfaces are on the bolt, so it is `structural` (kind `gap` is only for interfaces sharing no part), but it is `derived` in the same sense `shank_out` is: nothing in this repo sources this sub-region directly. `study_pitch_link_thread_region_t.json` computes it as `bolt_length_11 - fastener_grip`, reproducing the referenced stack's `thread_region_T` path exactly -- the stack's own notes call that quantity 'a provenance cross-check, not a design quantity', since it happens to equal NAS6403's T (Ref).

notes: This document adds no value, no citation and no confidence claim of its own. If a number here looks wrong, the stack file docs/tolerance_stacks/stack_pitch_link_to_pitch_plate.json is where it is wrong.

The graph: 6 parts, 9 interfaces, 10 edges, 3 branch points, 2 grounded loops (the clamped-stack/grip loop, and the length/grip/thread-region loop), 1 gap edge (`shank_out`; `thread_region` is derived but structural, since both its ends are on the bolt).

Until 2026-09-15 this graph was smaller: the pitch-link eye and the flanged-bushing flange were the joint's missing members, recorded in the checks' `excluded_terms` rather than modelled -- handoff stack_fable_audit added both to the stack (the eye as a loudly-marked placeholder) and this topology followed.

OPEN, for a future reviewer, exactly as topology_vpa_output_to_pitch_plate.json flags the same kind of question: this topology asserts an axial order for the clamped members (bushing, eye, flange, pitch-plate lug, washer, head-side first) taken from the stack's own element order and notes. The sum does not depend on it -- a chain sum is invariant to ordering -- but a reader looking at the rail diagram will read it as physical.
